findings.title: file_write has no upper bound on content size (DoS)
findings.rationale: file_read caps reads at 100 MB (ops.rs:140) and apply_patch caps the envelope at 4 MiB (apply_patch.rs:93), but file_write has no symmetric guard. A model that submits args.content as a multi-GB string allocates the full buffer before the deny-checked write ever begins; the path-lock + atomic_write_file pipeline then OOMs the worker, wedging the session. Same DoS class as the apply_patch finding already fixed in this same module.

findings.title: file_edit reads entire file into memory with no size cap
findings.rationale: file_read enforces `max_read_size = 100 MB` before allocation, but file_edit's read_text_file does an unbounded tokio::fs::read → String. A 2-GB text file causes a 2-GB allocation, which then OOMs the worker or stalls the writer for minutes. file_edit is LLM-callable, so a steered model has the same DoS vector as the apply_patch envelope (already capped). The cap should be applied at the same boundary as file_read for symmetry.

findings.title: PatchOp::Add body length is still uncapped (the MEDIUM follow-up from review batch 2 was not landed)
findings.rationale: The MAX_PATCH_BYTES envelope cap (4 MiB) was added in commit since 2026-08-11 review, but the per-op MEDIUM finding from that same review (`PatchOp::Add.lines` count and per-line size unbounded) was NOT addressed. A `*** Add File:` op with one million `+x` lines still parses into Vec<Line>, concatenates into one giant String, then writes. The envelope cap is only a coarse filter — within one envelope, a single op can still balloon memory and disk. Mirror the line count + body size cap that the review recommended.

findings.title: denied-paths enforcement can be bypassed via Add-onto-denied-parent (MEDIUM from review batch 2 unfixed)
findings.rationale: The batch-2 review flagged that `plan_add` relies on the resolve-step to deny-check, and recommended an explicit precheck that fails closed even when the denylist widens later. That fix was not landed. A `*** Add File: ~/.ssh/authorized_keys` op currently slips past only because the broad `/root/.ssh` (Unix) deny entry catches the canonicalized parent; an entry removal or a future config that drops `/etc/ssh` would silently re-open the gate. Pass denied_paths through to plan_add (and call path_is_denied directly on resolved) so the explicit precheck closes the dependency on prefix-only matches.

findings.title: Async line-counting loop holds the executor open on huge files; no spawn_blocking
findings.rationale: `count_lines` is called once per matched file in stats. The async BufReader::lines loop yields on every line — a per-line await on a hot path that does no I/O at all (the BufReader prefetches 8 KB at a time and `next_line()` just walks the cache). The pattern pins the worker through every iteration and serialises the entire stats walk onto a single tokio thread. Switching to a single spawn_blocking + std BufReader closes the per-line await storm and lets the executor keep making progress on other tasks while one stats walk runs. file_ops is a hot path; this is the only spot in this scope where per-line await is used.

findings.title: SpawnMeta depth is hard-coded to 1 for every delegation, including chained ones (review batch 3 still unfixed)
findings.rationale: The 2026-08-11 review (batch 3) explicitly recommended `depth = parent_depth + 1`. The fix was not landed (the constant `1` is still hardcoded at both lines 411 and 558). The background tracker's depth cap is the safety belt that refuses runaway delegation chains; underestimating depth by N means the chain can grow N deeper than the cap before the cap fires. Same finding still valid; not re-flagging for content, but tracking so the cluster is closed.

findings.title: note body size is uncapped at the dispatcher (DoS, review batch 5 still unfixed)
findings.rationale: The 2026-08-11 review (batch 5) recommended mirroring the read-side PER_NOTE_MAX_CHARS = 4_000 at the write site. Neither handle_create nor handle_update cap `args.content` today, so a 100 MB note is persisted on write and re-pays the full disk read + embedder + reparse-index cost on every subsequent page. Tracked here so the cluster is closed; fixing it is a 10-line patch that lands in note_manage/write.rs only.

findings.title: Per-line char-cost arithmetic allocates a Vec<String> even for the budget-bound early-break path
findings.rationale: Every file_read allocates one String per line for the rendered Vec, then `mint()` does another concat on the kept prefix. On a 2 000-line window that is up to 2 000 String allocations + one final concat of the whole prefix — measurable in flame graphs for read-heavy sessions. Building into a single String buffer via writeln! keeps the common case allocation-free beyond the buffer growths. file_ops is the hottest read path; this is the single biggest alloc hotspot in the module outside of `read_file_bytes` itself.

findings.title: Regex compile failure uses unreachable!() — startup panic if regex breaks
findings.rationale: Each Lazy<Regex> uses `unwrap_or_else(|e| unreachable!(...))`. The comment above claims a build-time check, but `unreachable!` is only reached on a regex engine change — not on a regex *edit*. If a future edit makes one of these patterns invalid (e.g. an unescaped `(`), the panic fires at first call, mid-extraction, with no link to the broken literal. Switch to a plain `.expect("static literal X")` so the panic message names the file:line + pattern and a CI build with `cargo test` flags it immediately. Not blocking; quality nit.

deferred.title: team/message_send.rs and team/task_submit.rs and team/task_comment.rs — payload fields have no per-call size cap
deferred.rationale: Same DoS class as the apply_patch / file_write findings. The 2026-08-11 review (batch 3) flagged this as Low and recommended a single 256 KiB constant at team/mod.rs. Worth a one-line patch but functionally similar to BTS-1 (file_write) so flagged here once, not duplicated as a separate BTS finding.

deferred.title: pdf_generate/* — `args.content` has no per-call size cap (review batch 6 still unfixed)
deferred.rationale: Both browser and native engines parse the full Markdown string before any output cap fires. 4 MiB constant recommended in batch 6; not yet landed. Tracked here as deferred so the existing review's cluster stays visible.

deferred.title: generation/{image,video,audio}_generate.rs — prompt has no upper bound (review batch 6 still unfixed)
deferred.rationale: The provider-side API usually has its own cap, but a runaway model can stuff a 100 MB prompt and pay for the request. 32 KiB constant at generation/mod.rs recommended in batch 6.

deferred.rationale: Performance nit only. 250 ms MIN_POLL_INTERVAL_MS would close it.
